833 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Watches for the south shore of Long Island on
Friday have been converted to Coastal Flood Advisories.

The ending time for the Wind Advisory has been changed to 1 AM. 
The High Wind Warning remains unchanged.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A major coastal storm will bring high winds, rain, and
coastal flooding to the area through this evening. 

2) Widespread moderate to major coastal flooding likely during
the evening high tide cycle. Minor to locally moderate impacts
possible during Friday AM high tide. Widespread beach flooding
and dune erosion also expected along the open water shorelines
during the times of high tide, with localized 
overwashes possible. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The combination of anomalously strong high pressure to the
northeast and low pressure tracking north across the Mid
Atlantic states will produce widespread rain and high winds
across the area through the first half tonight. An 80kt h-9 LLJ
over the region this evening combined with low level warming
will help to mix more of that momentum down to the surface, with
40-50kt winds likely at the coast until around 03Z before 
diminishing as a warm front moves into the area. A few higher
gusts are possible. The warm front will gradually lift north 
through the night along with rain and wind. 

Heaviest rain will also coincide with the strongest winds this
evening, with even a rumble of thunder possible. Rainfall
amounts are still expected to be in the 1-2 inch range with
localized higher amounts up to 3 inches. The system is 
progressive and hourly rates are unlikely to exceed an 
inch per hour. Any flooding should be mainly of the minor
nuisance variety. There is a low probability of flash flooding.

Temperatures will gradually rise into the 50s through the night,
especially with the passage of the warm front. A period of fog
may also be possible overnight as winds slacken with the warm 
front and dew points increase. Southerly winds do gradually 
increase after this lull from south to north.

The low occludes passes to west tonight into Friday, passing to
the north Friday night into Saturday. The associated upper low
passes to the northwest on Friday with plenty of cloud cover 
and chances of showers. The best chance will be to the north and
west of NYC. Highs will top out in the mid to upper 50s. MAV 
MOS and CONSALL are cooler and that is a possibility with the 
cloud cover and the coverage of showers. S-SW winds will gust
25-30 mph. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Coastal flood warning remains up for tonight with the exception
of SE CT. The coastal flood watch for the south shore of Long
Island for Sunday has been converted to an advisory. Thus, a
coastal flood advisory is in effect for all locations 
on Sunday. 

While most locations need only an additional foot of tidal
departure to reach coastal flood benchmarks tonight, this will 
be offset by the highest winds during the nighttime hours. 
Much of the surge guidance is pointing to a 3-4 ft surge with
widespread moderate to major coastal flooding. In many cases, 
water levels have ticked up a bit with our latest forecast. 

The storm surge will be driven by storm force ENE winds through
the first half of tonight due to the strong pressure gradient 
between low pressure to the southwest and high pressure to the
north. Other areas of note for significant impacts will be the
Peconic Bay area with funneling of surge toward the Peconic
River, and along the western Long Island LI Sound shoreline with
moderate water levels combined with high wave action. 

Surge up tidally affected rivers (Hackensack, Hudson, and
Passaic) will result in minor to moderate flooding as well, 
especially during tonight's high tide cycle. 

For the Friday AM high tides, winds switch to the southwest with
widespread minor flooding likely. Localized moderate flooding is
possible in the south shore back of bays of Long Island. 
In general, the fcst has been lowered except for the back bays 
where the SW flow may slightly redistribute impacts.

For the oceanfront, breaking waves of 8-12 ft will result in 
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high 
tide. There is potential for localized overwashes, exacerbating 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective
dunes. Along the western Sound and the forks of Long Island,
breaking waves of 3-6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion
and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective
dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to 
shoreline and marina structures as well.

Heavy rain coinciding with the evening high tides could
exacerbate street flooding issues along the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...

**HIGH IMPACT STORM TONIGHT**

A large storm will continue to move across the Mid Atlantic
states, passing to the W late tonight. An associated warm front
will approach this evening and LIft north overnight. 

Winds out of the ENE are at their peak this evening (25-35 kt
with gusts 40-50 kt, highest at the NYC metro and Long Island 
terminals. Peak gusts could be a few kt higher. This will also 
be accompanied by easterly LLWS at 50-70 kt at 1500-2000 ft AGL.
Winds diminish overnight and eventually become S-SW 10-15 kt 
with gusts up to 20 kt. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Unscheduled AMD possible to address changes in flight category
and winds. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 00Z Saturday through Tuesday... 

Friday night: VFR. SW winds G20kt becoming W after midnight. 

Saturday: VFR. W winds G20-25kt, diminishing at night. 

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night: Showers likely with MVFR cond after midnight. 

Monday: Chance of morning showers with MVFR cond. SW winds
G20-25kt, becoming W in the afternoon and NW at night.

Tuesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
No changes to the Gale and Storm Warnings. Seas on the ocean are 
modeled to build to around 20 ft at the height of the storm in the 
late aftn and eve, with waves on the Sound and the NY Harbor 
entrance up to around 10 ft. ENE winds will frequently gust in
the 50-60 kt range this evening before weakening with a warm 
frontal passage later tonight.

Conditions improve a little on Fri, but a SW gale is likely on
the ocean and maybe on some of the non-ocean waters as well. 
Winds diminish to SCA lvls on Sat in a westerly flow, and likely
blw SCA lvls on Sun. A frontal sys on Mon could produce SW-W 
gales on the ocean with SCA conditions elsewhere.
